steps: Plan the location & design option

Pick standard, Komfort Zone Kit, heat transfer kit(s) or Kozy Power Vent first: framing, clearances and venting follow from it. Level base that carries the unit and vent; 84" minimum enclosure and ceiling height.

• Read all documentation for your installation and design options first. KZK-062 (combustible facing above, heat reduction for a TV, lower mantel clearances) and HTK-EXT / HTK-INT have their own manuals and may change framing; up to (2) heat transfer kits can be fitted.
  • Kozy Power Vent (#KPV): fan-powered mechanical draft, horizontal terminations only; see its manual.
  • Install on a level surface able to support the fireplace and venting. The fireplace isn't load-bearing; framing, facing and finishing must be self-supported.
  • Set it directly on wood or a non-combustible surface. On carpeting, tile or other combustibles other than wood, use a metal or wood panel the full width and depth. Above floor level, build a solid, continuous platform.
  • Fireplace chamber and ceiling: 84" (2134mm) minimum height, standard and KZK.
  • Out of traffic, away from furniture and draperies; a bedroom is allowed. Outdoor covered installation (protected from direct precipitation): operation approved from 40°F to 110°F (4°C to 43°C); black painted safety barriers recommended.
  • Propane? Converting before setting the unit in the framed opening is easier.
Frame the opening
Frame to Figure 3.5 (the same rough-in for every design option) on nominal 2" x 4" framing, allowing for wall covering and facing thickness. Lay out the vent path before setting the unit.

Minimum framing is shown only in Figure 3.5 (p. 18), appliance dimensions in Figure 2.2 (p. 10) and the wall thimble rough-in in Figure 3.8 (p. 21, measured with Simpson DuraVent pipe). All three are diagrams: read them from the PDF.

  • Cold air transfer area: the enclosure must meet every clearance and local building codes; insulate outside walls.
  • Leave room in front for barrier removal, component access, gas line installation and service.
  • Masonry: a foundation for the full load, and a lintel over the appliance.
  • TV above: the KZK option is highly recommended, with its plenum discharge above the TV and a mantel. The allowed TV recess is 4-1/4" (108mm), from the front of the 2x4 framing to the back of the pocket's finishing material.
  • Exterior termination location must meet Section 7.2 (see the Vent termination card).
Top stand-offs & nailing flanges

Do any KZK or heat transfer kit prep first. Attach the top stand-off brackets ((4) screws) and horizontal heat shields ((8) screws), which hold the 10-7/8" header clearance, then fit both nailing flanges with the stand-off flanges facing out.

1. KZK: remove the (16) screws and the (2) top cover plates (discard the plates), fit the KZK collars with those screws, then remove and discard the (3) convection baffles and their screws. HTK: remove the side HTK cover plate ((4) screws) and the lifting handle ((9) screws), then fit the HTK-NTL air chute and its collar; the damper stays for HTK-EXT and comes out for HTK-INT.
  2. Attach the top stand-off brackets to the top of the fireplace with (4) screws. Bend up the screw-hole tabs of the horizontal heat shields and attach them with (8) screws.
  3. Remove the (2) nailing flanges, align them with the holes on the outside corners, stand-off flanges facing away from the fireplace, and screw them on through the slots.
  4. Bend the perforation until it's parallel with the fireplace face, never toward it.
Non-combustible material only in the header zone above the stand-offs, the full width of the fireplace: no wood or sheetrock. Never permanently remove the stand-off or flange assemblies.
Note: p. 13 says KZK / HTK preparation must be completed before setting the appliance in the framed opening, but the HTK preparation steps recommend installing the fireplace in the framed opening before removing the lifting handle (p. 26).
Set & secure the fireplace
Team-lift it by the side lift handles (a 2" x 4" fits through them), set it in the framed opening flush with the framing, and secure the framing to the nailing flanges.

• The appliance is heavy: use a team lift to move, place and position it. The lift handles on both sides take a hand lift or a 2" x 4" through them.
  • Position a framing stud against the small stand-off on the back of each nailing flange and secure it with nails or screws. The flanges hold the minimum 4" (102mm) from the fireplace sides to framing; the stand-off brackets themselves need 0".
  • Next, per the manual's general procedure: KZK (if used), vent pipe, gas line, electrical wiring, then finishing material.
Vent heat shield, restrictor & vent

Fit the required vent heat shield(s) and the restrictor plate before attaching vent. 5" x 8" co-axial from an approved maker; 1/4" rise per 12" on horizontal runs; 11-3/8" above horizontal pipe in the chamber, 1" elsewhere.

• Vent heat shields are required in all venting scenarios: the front vertical shield alone when the pipe terminates at the enclosure ceiling; front vertical plus top horizontal shield when it terminates at the wall at the minimum vent run (Figure 3.7, p. 18).
  • Restrictor plate (components packet): install per Figure 7.3 before attaching venting; fine-tune later per 11.2.3.
  • Wall thimbles that keep the 1" (25mm) top clearance are required wherever a horizontal run passes through a wall; they and attic insulation shields may be insulated with unfaced non-combustible insulation (ASTM E 136).
  • Elbow heights vary by vent maker: adjust the thimble rough opening to keep clearances. After the thimble, keep 1" (25mm) on all surfaces of the pipe.
  • Don't recess the vent cap into the wall or siding. Leave a way to visually check the vent connection after installation.
  • Runs, elbows and termination limits: see the Venting and Vent termination cards.
Gas line + leak test

Ships for natural gas: convert first if using propane. Run the line through the gas line hole, clear of the fan, with a listed ½" tee-handle shut-off and flexible connector to the ½" valve inlet. Leak-test every joint with soapy water.

• Qualified person only, to local codes or ANSI Z223.1; in Massachusetts, a licensed plumber or gas fitter.
  • The fireplace comes with a 3/8" (10mm) x 18" (457mm) flexible gas connector and manual shut-off valve. Substituting? Check local codes.
  • Line pressure tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa): disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve. At ½ psi or less: isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.
  • Supply pressure: natural gas 5" WC min (7" WC recommended), 10" WC max; propane 11" WC min, 13" WC max.
  • High altitude: consult the local gas distributor or authority having jurisdiction for rating methods.
  • Before start-up, check all connections, field or factory made, with soapy water.
Electrical
120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amps to the junction box, hot at all times with no switch in the supply. Plug into a properly grounded three-prong receptacle; ground per local codes, ANSI/NFPA 70 or CSA C22.1.

• Shut off the household breaker before working on any electrical lines. Never cut or remove the grounding prong.
  • Fan kit #SL42-028 (optional, qualified installer only): two fans, one per fan channel with the motor toward the center; the cord plugs into the receptacle on the IFC control module. Don't let a fan rest on electrical cords.
  • Spade connectors are labeled "M" (male) and "F" (female). Wiring diagrams: Figures 9.1 to 9.3 (p. 56 to 58).
  • Outdoor installations: wiring to the outdoor requirements of NECA NFPA 70.
Facing, finishing & mantel

Non-combustible (ASTM E 136) material only where Figure 5.6 calls for it. Combustible mantel: 6" deep starting 12-1/2" above the top finishing edge, then 1" deeper per 1" higher; sidewall from 3"; hearth unlimited from 0".

• Paper-faced gypsum board (drywall, including Type X) and WonderBoard backerboard are not non-combustible materials.
  • Non-combustible mantel: up to 8" (203mm) deep at 0" from the top finishing edge, then 1" up for every 1" deeper. Non-combustible surround: up to 8" (203mm) at 0" from the side and top finishing edges.
  • Finishing material can't obstruct ventilation air. Figure 5.6 (p. 34, a diagram) also marks where screws aren't allowed.
  • Optional rectangle surround #NK48TL-RS covers the finishing edge on all 4 sides and takes up to 1-5/8" (41mm) of non-combustible facing plus finishing material.
  • Against cracking above the unit: dry, dust-free materials; heat-resilient tape, mesh and joint compound (such as Durabond), cured per its maker; a quality acrylic latex primer and finish, avoiding flat or light colors. Never a one-piece U-shaped stone surround; stone must tolerate more than 160°F.
Light kits, logs, glass & screen

Convert to propane first if needed. Fit the (7) halogen bulbs in the front bottom light kit (not installed at the factory), then the optional panel set and the log set, refit the glass and hang the safety screen.

• Disconnect power. Never touch halogen bulbs with bare hands; use a soft cloth. Front kit: lift out the front ember media tray ((2) screws), install the bulbs, refit the tray. The back bottom and top light kits come with their bulbs installed.
  • The optional panel set goes in before the logs. Log set per its own instructions: Traditional #NK48TL-500 or Birch #NK48TL-B501.
  • Glass: reverse the removal steps (support rail at the bottom; (4) spring-loaded latches at the top, worked with the glass latch tool).
  • Safety screen barrier #NK48TL-ES must be installed: align its hooks with the slots on each side, between the glass frame and the side finishing edge, then lift and push it in so they latch around the glass frame. Even spacing to the finishing edges on all four sides means it's seated.
Initialize, pressure-test & check flames

Rocker switch OFF, (3) AAA in the remote, plug in, clear the firebox. Press the remote sync button (3 beeps, amber LED), then remote ON/OFF within 5 seconds (4 beeps, pilot lights), ON/OFF again, rocker ON. Check inlet and manifold pressures; burn 15 minutes, then adjust venturis or the restrictor plate.

1. Rocker switch OFF; (3) AAA batteries in the remote; connect the IFC module to AC power. Remove all packaging and combustible material from the firebox: the next steps spark the pilot.
  2. Remove the safety screen and component access cover. Press the remote sync button (SW1, red): 3 beeps and an amber LED.
  3. Within 5 seconds press ON/OFF on the remote: 4 beeps, and the pilot lights. Press it again: the pilot goes out. The system is initialized.
  4. Rocker switch ON; refit the cover and screen.
  5. Pressures: manometer on a 1/4" (6mm) I.D. hose at the IN tap (other gas appliances on) and at the OUT tap on low and high; reseal each tap snug and confirm it reads no pressure.
  6. Flames start blue and turn yellow over the first 15 minutes. Venturis are factory set; any adjustment is for a qualified service technician, in slight increments, burning at least 15 minutes and cooling between changes. If soot shows, check media placement first.
Lazy, yellow flamesideal; no adjustment
Short, blue flamesventuris too open: close slightly
Dark orange, black tipsventuris closed too far: open slightly
Active, compact flame (vertical runs)install or modify the restrictor plate
Note: p. 69 says opening the air shutter gives a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner, and the troubleshooting chart says to close the shutter slightly for a blue flame that lifts (p. 75); but Figure 11.3 says lifting (ghosting) flames mean the venturis are closed too far and should be opened slightly, or that the gas pressure is too high, measured with a manometer (p. 70).

panels.title: Pilot won't light, stay lit or go out
items: Power interrupted or disconnected → restore power, or use the battery backup with fully charged batteries
Wiring disconnected → check every connection against the wiring schematic (Section 9.0)
Gas supply off → check the shut-off valves; there may be more than one between appliance and main line
No propane, or low gas pressure (bent line, too-narrow pipe, low line pressure) → refill the tank; consult a plumber or gas supplier
Pilot adjustment screw not sealed → seal it; don't over-tighten
Pilot not contacting the flame rectification sensor → it must envelop the top of the sensor and reach far enough onto the burner
Pilot always on, won't go out → control is in CPI mode; set it to IPI

panels.title: Burner won't light, or remote does nothing
items: ON/OFF rocker switch OFF → switch it ON
Gas supply off or low → check for multiple shut-offs and the propane tank; consult a plumber or gas supplier
Wiring disconnected or improper → check against Section 9.0
Plugged burner orifice → remove the blockage
Pilot not directed to ignite the burner → see the pilot causes
No call for heat → remote powered ON and thermostat operation OFF; replace remote batteries
No reaction to the SIT remote → replace remote or backup batteries, reprogram the remote to the IFC module, or reset the IFC after too many failed ignitions

panels.title: Pilot & burner go out while running
items: Glass assembly installed incorrectly → refit per Section 8.1
Vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked → adjust; remove debris
Horizontal vent without 1/4" (6mm) rise per 12" (305mm) of travel → correct the pitch
Exhaust pipe leaking exhaust gases back into the firebox → find and repair leaks
Excessive draft → install or modify the restrictor plate (11.2.3)

panels.title: Blue, lifting flames or soot on glass
items: Blue flame lifting off the burner → chart: close the venturi air shutter slightly (Figure 11.3 disagrees; see the last install step)
Blue, lifting flame: vent cap wrong, vent leaking or cap blocked → adjust; repair leaks; remove debris
Soot on glass → check log placement and burner / perimeter media placement
Soot on glass, improper venturi setting → open the air shutter slightly for more air
Soot on glass, vent cap wrong or blocked → adjust; remove debris

codes: Backup pack below 4V; low double-beep on ON/OFF and no commands accepted. Replace the batteries.
No flame after 2 ignition tries. Verify gas is on and the sensor isn't shorted; reset (OFF, wait about 2 seconds, ON) or re-initialize (10.2).

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
Your fireplace lights itself: an igniter sparks the pilot, and the pilot lights the burner. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Every day

Press ON/OFF on the remote. The fireplace beeps once, and about 4 seconds later it starts sparking at the pilot. Press ON/OFF again to turn it off. The main ON/OFF rocker switch, behind the component access cover, must be ON for the remote to work.

If it doesn't light

The control makes 2 tries, sparking about 60 seconds each, with about 35 seconds between. Then it locks out, and its red light blinks 3 times at intervals. To reset, press ON/OFF to turn the system off, wait about 2 seconds, and press it again.

The full lighting steps

  1. Press OFF on the remote, then turn off all electric power to the fireplace.
  2. Turn the manual gas valve clockwise to OFF. Wait 5 minutes, then smell for gas, including near the floor. If you smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps under Safety.
  3. If you don't, turn the valve counterclockwise to ON, turn the power back on, and press ON on the remote.
Still won't work? Press OFF on the remote, turn the manual valve clockwise to OFF, and call your service technician or gas supplier. Turn the valve by hand only, never with tools. If it won't turn by hand, don't try to repair it: call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The remote takes 3 AAA batteries. The fireplace answers each command with a single beep.

  • ON/OFF: turns the fireplace on and off.
  • Up / Down arrows: flame height, in 6 levels. Down lowers it one level at a time until the flame is off; Up raises it. If the system is on but the flame is off, Up relights it on HI.
  • Thermostat key: press it once and the remote works as a room thermostat, showing the room and set temperatures; the arrows change the set temperature. Press it until SMART shows and the fireplace turns its flame down by itself as the room reaches your setting. You can't adjust the flame by hand while Smart is on.
  • Mode key: steps to the fan, top light and AUX (ember bed light) settings.

Handy extras

  • Key lock against unsupervised use: press Mode and Up together. A lock icon shows; repeat to unlock.
  • °F or °C: with the system off, press Thermostat and Mode together.
  • Low batteries: a battery icon shows before they run out.
No remote? Remove the safety screen and component access cover, slide out the control module and set the rocker switch OFF. Hold the remote sync button until it beeps 3 times, then press it again within 5 seconds. The pilot lights, and the rocker switch now turns the burner on (HI only) and off.

normal.title: That's probably normal
normal.html:
Blue flames at first

When the fireplace is first lit, the flames look blue. Over the first 15 minutes they gradually turn yellow. If they stay blue, or turn dark orange with black tips (soot), the burner's air shutters may need adjusting. That's a job for a qualified service technician.

Noise as it heats and cools

Some parts expand, contract and move slightly, and that makes noise. The warranty calls this, and some discoloring, normal and not a defect.

The pilot goes out on its own

  • When the pilot has been lit continuously, the control turns the fireplace off for about 5 seconds within 24 hours as a safety check, then repeats your last command.
  • In CPI (standing pilot) mode, the pilot turns off after 7 days in a row without the main burner lighting. That's a standard safety feature.

The fan keeps running

In thermostat mode the fan starts 5 minutes after the fire lights and keeps going about 12 minutes after it's off.

A gas smell is different. If you smell gas, don't light anything or touch any switch. Leave the building and immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Cleaning the glass is your once-a-year job. Do it only when the fireplace is completely cool: never remove or clean the glass while it's hot.

  1. Clear a flat, stable work surface big enough to lay the glass assembly on.
  2. Lift the safety screen up and out of its slots.
  3. Find the 4 spring-loaded latches at the top of the firebox. With the glass latch tool from the components packet, pull each latch out and up to free the top of the glass.
  4. Tilt the top of the glass toward you and lift it off the support rail at the bottom.
  5. Clean it with a fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Never use abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  6. Put the glass back in reverse order. Rehang the screen so its hooks latch around the glass frame; the gap to the fireplace edges should be even all around.
Never run the fireplace with the glass off, cracked or broken, or without the safety screen. Don't strike or slam the glass. A damaged glass assembly should be replaced by a qualified service person.
Note: the manual's glass removal steps put the latches at the top of the firebox (p. 46), but its yearly service list mentions a bottom latch assembly (p. 72).

pilot.title: Pilot modes: IPI or CPI
pilot.html:
The pilot can run two ways, and you choose on the remote.

IPI: spark to pilot

The igniter lights the pilot each time the fireplace turns on. With the fireplace on, the screen shows no snowflake icon.

CPI: continuous (standing) pilot

The pilot stays lit. That keeps the firebox warm and starts a draft in the vent, so the burner lights with less disruption to the air flow. With the fireplace on, the screen shows a snowflake icon. If the main burner doesn't light for 7 days in a row, the pilot turns itself off, a standard safety feature. Each time the burner lights, the 7 days start over.

To switch

  1. Turn the fireplace off with the remote.
  2. Press Mode until the CPI icon shows.
  3. Press Up for CPI, or Down for IPI. A single beep confirms.
Pilot lit all the time and won't go out? The system is set to CPI. Switch it to IPI.

power.title: Power outages & batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on household power (120 VAC), with a backup battery pack for outages.

In a power outage

The burner still lights and you can still change the flame height, running on the backup batteries. The fan and accent lights won't work until the power is back.

Low-battery signs

Remote (3 AAA)Battery icon on the screen
Backup battery packRed light blinks once at intervals; a low double-beep when you press ON/OFF

After the backup pack's low-battery alert, the fireplace won't accept any commands until you replace those batteries. Once they're replaced, it beeps as soon as it has power.

How long batteries last depends on their quality and how often the fireplace lights; for the remote, also on how often you change the thermostat setting.

lights.title: Fan & lights
lights.html:
The fan and lights run on household power only. In an outage the burner keeps working on the backup batteries, but these don't.

Fan (optional kit)

Press Mode until the fan icon shows, then use the arrows to turn it on, off, or through its 6 speeds.

  • Thermostat mode: the fan waits 5 minutes after the fireplace lights, so heat can build, and runs about 12 minutes after it turns off.
  • Manual mode: it runs at your last setting, with no delay starting or stopping.

Top accent light

Press Mode until the light icon shows, then use the arrows to pick one of 6 brightness levels.

Ember bed light

Press Mode until AUX shows. Up turns it on, Down turns it off. To change its brightness, lift the safety screen up and out of its slots, remove the component access cover, and turn the knob under the firebox: clockwise is brighter, counterclockwise dimmer. Put both back afterward.

Each feature can be switched on (SEL) or off (CLR) in the remote's setup. If its icon never shows, the setup steps are on pages 65 to 67 of the manual.

safety.title: Safety & gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building right away.
  • Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Before lighting, smell all around the fireplace, including next to the floor: some gas is heavier than air and settles there.

Hot glass and children

Hot glass will burn. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it. Keep the safety screen on: it's there to protect children and other at-risk people. If it's damaged, replace it with the maker's screen for this fireplace. Watch young children closely in the same room, and consider a safety gate to keep toddlers away from hot surfaces.

Every day

  • Keep clothing and anything flammable off and away from it, and never store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors or liquids nearby.
  • Don't use it if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the fireplace and replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.
  • Turn the gas valve by hand only, never with tools. If it won't turn by hand, don't try to repair it: call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.

service.title: Yearly service
service.html:
Have the fireplace inspected by a professional service person before use and at least once a year. Lint from carpeting, bedding or pets can mean cleaning more often.

What the yearly visit covers

  • Vacuuming the firebox, burners, control compartment and air passages, and the fan (its bearings are sealed and need no oil).
  • Checking the vent and vent cap for soot or blockage, and that combustion and ventilation air flow freely.
  • Checking gas tubes and connections for leaks, and the pilot and burner: the burner should light within 4 seconds of the gas valve opening, with steady flames that don't lift or float.
  • Inspecting the glass for cracks, scratches and nicks, and checking that its spring-loaded latches move freely. The glass and latches are the fireplace's pressure-relief mechanism.
  • Replacing light bulbs as needed.

Your part

Clean the glass once a year, and keep the area around the fireplace clear of anything that burns.

Anything taken apart for service, from wiring to the vent, must go back exactly as the instructions say, and a safety screen removed for service goes back on before the fireplace is used.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg. warrants this Kozy Heat fireplace to the original purchaser, from the date of purchase, against defects in materials and workmanship. It's a limited lifetime warranty and can't be transferred.

30 days · parts and laborPaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1 · parts and laborAll other parts and material
Years 2 to lifetime · parts onlyFirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shields, front glass (thermal shock only), refractory liner (not enamel or glass panels)

Labor is paid to authorized dealers only. Nothing needs to be sent in to register: keep your proof of purchase with the model and serial number. If you notice a defect, contact your authorized dealer within 30 days.

What voids it

  • Installation by anyone but a licensed, authorized technician or contractor, or not installing, running and maintaining it per the manual.
  • A removed serial number or testing label, or any alteration.
  • Submersion, long dampness or condensation, or water damage from improper venting.
This is a summary. The full terms and exclusions are in the official PDF.

specInput.title: Input rates & orifices
specInput.html:

LP max / min51,000 / 40,000 Btu/h (14.95 / 11.72 kW)

Burner positions (Left, Center, Right, Bottom) are identified in Figure 2.1 (p. 9).

High altitude

US: above 2,000' (610m), reduce input ratings 4% for each 1,000' (305m) above sea level. Canada: above 4,500' (1,372m), reduce the certified high-altitude rating 4% for each additional 1,000' (305m). Also follow ANSI Z223.1/NFPA 54, CSA-B149.1 and local authorities on derating.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas min5" WC (1.25 kPa) · 7" WC (1.74 kPa) recommended
Natural gas max10" WC (2.49 kPa)
Propane min / max11" WC (2.74 kPa) / 13" WC (3.24 kPa)

Inlet test, IN tap (p. 68)

  1. Test with all other gas appliances in the house on, at full capacity.
  2. Loosen the IN tap screw counter-clockwise; attach a manometer with a 1/4" (6mm) I.D. hose.
  3. Light pilot and burners; the reading must fall between the minimum and maximum.
  4. Burners and pilot off; remove the hose and tighten the tap clockwise, snug, not over-tight.
  5. Relight and reattach the manometer: it should read no pressure, proving the tap is sealed.

Too high or too low: contact the gas company; only a qualified gas service technician adjusts incoming pressure. Line pressure tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa): disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve; at ½ psi or less, close its manual shut-off valve.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
Natural gas high / low3.5" WC (0.87 kPa) / 1.6" WC (0.40 kPa)
Propane high / low10" WC (2.49 kPa) / 6.4" WC (1.59 kPa)

Manifold test, OUT tap (p. 68)

  1. Light the pilot; loosen the OUT tap screw counter-clockwise.
  2. Attach a manometer with a 1/4" (6mm) I.D. hose.
  3. Light the burners; read at the low and high settings.
  4. Burners and pilot off; remove the hose and tighten the tap clockwise, snug, not over-tight.
  5. Reattach the manometer: no pressure with pilot and burner on means it's sealed.

Both taps are on the valve: OUT measures outgoing (manifold) pressure, IN incoming.

specVent.title: Venting (natural draft)
specVent.html:

Approved makers, horizontal and vertical: American Metal Products (Ameri-Vent), BDM, ICC, Metal Fab., Selkirk and Simpson DuraVent; cap part numbers in Tables 7.2 and 7.3. ICC TM-5HT and TM-4HT caps require ICC wind / heat shield HTS. Natural gas and propane follow the same rules.

conflicts.issue: Reduced 4" x 6-5/8" venting: 7.6.2 says it is only approved for vertical terminations (excluding #KPV), but 7.7.2 (v) lists a basement horizontal install (36" 5"x8" vertical + 4" x 6-5/8" reducer + 90° elbow + 24" max horizontal + cap) and Fig. 7.7 is titled '5"x8" and Reduced 4"x6-5/8" Horizontal Terminations'.

Venturi direction for lifting flames: 11.2.1 says opening the air shutter gives a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner, and the troubleshooting chart says close the shutter slightly for a flame that burns blue and lifts; Fig. 11.3 says lifting (ghosting) flames mean the venturis are closed too far (open slightly) or gas pressure is too high.

Heat transfer kit prep timing: 3.4 says KZK/HTK preparation (Section 4.0) must be completed before setting the appliance in the framed opening; the 4.2 HTK note recommends installing the fireplace in the framed opening before removing the lifting handle, which HTK prep steps 2-3 require.

Glass latch location: 8.1.1 removal steps use (4) spring-loaded latches at the top of the firebox (glass lifts off a bottom support rail); the 12.1 annual service list says to inspect and operate the 'bottom latch assembly' of the glass frame.

review.notes: Section banners and the table of contents (p. 5) are images; pages 2, 4, 6 and 82 have no text. Shown only as diagrams, so not transcribed (the guide names the figure and page): appliance dimensions Fig. 2.2 (p. 10), safety screen dimensions Fig. 2.3 (p. 11), minimum framing Fig. 3.5 (p. 18), wall thimble rough-in Fig. 3.8 (p. 21), non-combustible facing zone and no-screw areas Fig. 5.6 (p. 34; a lone 65-1/2" label isn't explained in the text), termination locations Fig. 7.2 (p. 37), combination-venting shaded area Fig. 7.8 (p. 44), correct pilot/burner flame photos (p. 74). Tables 11.1-11.5 (pressure, venturi and vent-restriction tables cited on p. 68-71) are not in the text; the guide uses the p. 8 spec table and Table 6.1 (p. 35). Catalog checks: BTU (NG 51,000/34,000, LP 51,000/40,000), 5 x 8 vent, IPI ignition, optional blower, 4 x 6-5/8 reduction for vertical and Class A/masonry conversion all match the manual. Not in the manual text, so not compared: efficiency (71.62% NG / 72.07% LP AFUE), height/width/depth, weight (335 lb) and view area (48" x 20"; the manual only lists the 49-5/8" x 22-1/8" glass part, p. 79). The backup battery pack's battery type, count and location aren't stated anywhere in the text, so the guide doesn't name them. The lighting label (p. 59) calls the pilot 'on-demand' and says it shuts off after 7 days; p. 60 ties the 7-day shutoff to CPI mode; the guide follows p. 60. Troubleshooting rows on p. 75-76 don't group unambiguously in the text (which issue 'Low gas pressure' and the second 'No propane in tank' belong to), so the guide merges pilot won't-light / won't-stay-lit into one panel and leaves 'No propane in tank' out of the goes-out-while-running panel. Parts list p. 78: the S.I.T. board assemblies (NG/LP) and transmitter numbers (N48TL-130, 700-248, 700-408) and the unlabeled 700-264 and 900-007 can't be matched to items reliably from the text; not used. 3.9.6 says to frame the thimble so the vent can 'run level' through it while horizontal sections need 1/4" rise per 12" (p. 20, 39, 42); treated as wording, not flagged. 50' is given as 15.24m (p. 41, 45) and 15.2m (p. 44): metric rounding only. The 'No remote?' note follows the unlabeled second procedure on p. 60 (sync button held, pressed again within 5 seconds; burner on HI only from the rocker switch).
